assumptions: Polish legal and clinical review permits the proposed clinic-supervised operating structure.
A licensed medical partner will contract for ordering, oversight, interpretation, and escalation at a sustainable per-study cost.
Clinic referral density can keep a small device fleet sufficiently utilized.
Adequate-study and repeat rates support the wholesale price after all logistics and support costs.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Applicable Polish regulatory guidance, device lease and maintenance quotes, physician cost, clinic minimum-volume commitments, observed utilization and failed-study rates, end-to-end turnaround, and per-study contribution after acquisition and compliance overhead.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Pooling devices, logistics, technical-quality checks, and contracted interpretation can remove clinic capex and scheduling friction, but it is a conventional capacity-service model without evidence of a uniquely underserved constraint.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Published prices prove that patients buy home sleep studies, but they do not establish clinic demand for outsourced wholesale capacity, referral density, waitlist pain, or a margin-preserving willingness to pay.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: The 300-450 PLN wholesale hypothesis must absorb interpretation, courier, consumables, cleaning, support, failed repeats, acquisition, depreciation, compliance, and idle time, leaving economics highly exposed to utilization.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Small private clinics lacking their own device workflow form a legible regional beachhead and sleep testing is an established paid event, but the number of suitable clinics and unmet referral volume are unknown.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Hospitals, private chains, CPAP vendors, telemedicine providers, and clinics can own or source the same devices and interpretation, while the venture controls neither referrals nor a scarce asset.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A dense local operation could add devices, clinics, cities, CPAP monitoring, and adjacent home diagnostics, but growth remains constrained by regulated labor, logistics, referral density, and equipment utilization.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Operational data may reduce failed studies and improve routing, but devices and clinical partners are replaceable, clinics own the patient relationship, and no exclusive referral or medical-services contract exists.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Data skills fit utilization and quality analysis, but the founder lacks medical credentials, clinic access, devices, referral rights, and a contracted physician, leaving the core operating advantages hypothetical.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Existing paid home-testing offers validate acceptance of the modality, yet the packet provides no evidence of a new capacity shortage, reimbursement change, or demand acceleration favoring a standalone pool now.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Clinic contracts, physician referrals, and CPAP partnerships are sensible concentrated routes, but all require trust and clinical alignment and none is currently secured.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A small fleet fits the capital envelope, but patient safety, health data, device compliance, failed recordings, licensed interpretation, courier coordination, and part-time oversight make reliable delivery difficult.

highest_value_structural_change: Secure a minimum-volume clinic capacity contract and lease devices only against that committed demand, with the clinic retaining all medical ordering and interpretation and the venture paid for technically adequate turnaround.
main_structural_strength: A clinic-facing capacity service can combine a proven paid diagnostic event with asset sharing, sparing small clinics from buying and operating their own device fleet.
primary_score_limiter: The proposed wholesale price has no demonstrated room for specialist, logistics, failure, compliance, acquisition, and idle-capacity costs, and no clinic demand is evidenced.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Published consumer prices are already low while clinics and existing providers can add the same devices directly, undermining both contribution margin and differentiation.
